newsitem.title: FRANCE: CDC state bank gets 90.59 pct Cr Foncier.
newsitem.headline: CDC state bank gets 90.59 pct Cr Foncier.

text.p: The takeover bid for Credit Foncier, launched by the CDC state bank on the French government's behalf under a plan to wind down the property lender, got acceptances representing 90.59 percent of the capital, the SBF stock markets association said on Monday.
An SBF statement said the acceptances registered on December 4, closing date for the offer, totalled 34,161,203 shares, or 90.59 percent of the capital.
An SBF spokesman, replying to a question from Reuters, said the CDC had to get upwards of 95 percent if it wanted to launch a buyout of remaining minority shareholders.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis announced plans in July for a "managed wind-down" of Credit Foncier after the group reported a 1995 loss of 10.8 billion francs.
The first stage of his wind-down plan was a takeover by the state-owned bank Caisses des Depots et Consignations (CDC).

His plan is to spin off the management of existing housing loans business to Credit Immobilier and create a state holding company to take care of the outstanding bond obligations of Credit Foncier, the second biggest bond issuer after the state.
The wind-down plan has run into stiff resistance from trade unions and politicians who allege the accounts were deliberately overloaded with provisions.

Their case gained momentum last week when it emerged that Credit Foncier was expecting to make a profit of around one billion francs in 1996 after a surprise profit of more than 400 million francs in the first half.
Arthuis will be questioned by the National Assembly finance committee on Tuesday afternoon before a decision on a petition by around 100 parliamentarians for the creation of a commission of inquiry.
Arthuis was in Nuremberg on Monday for the meeting between President Jacques Chirac and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and expected back late in the evening.
